MUS-01.direction: A space portfolio that grows from quiet scale into a substantial reveal.
MUS-01.why: Wide image and a large loudness range support chapter contrast; the restrained top end need not compete with tiny graphic details.
MUS-01.avoid: The title does not mean a uniformly quiet bed. Do not cut to every detected attack.
MUS-01.history: User-selected for the Sobiverse space portfolio.

MUS-02.direction: A concise launch, kinetic title sequence or one-minute graphic reel.
MUS-02.why: Relatively bright spectrum, frequent attack candidates and strong pulse autocorrelation give useful places to test short graphic accents.
MUS-02.avoid: Only 63 seconds long; it cannot cover a two-minute film unchanged. Confirm the pulse by audition before timing text to it.

MUS-03.direction: A precise product film with a steady feature section and a later escalation.
MUS-03.why: The low-variation 30-second passage and a pronounced later rise support both readable specifications and a second-act reveal.
MUS-03.avoid: Do not treat its whole three minutes as one even loop; the strongest measured rise is well into the source.
MUS-03.history: Latest user-selected music for the realme Make it real film; source 0–120s.

MUS-04.direction: A material-focused reveal: macro texture, deliberate negative space, then a larger product view.
MUS-04.why: Very restrained spectral brightness and a 15LU loudness range favour contrast between close detail and a reveal.
MUS-04.avoid: Not a constant low-level luxury bed; use a bounded passage and plan for its large level changes.

MUS-05.direction: A distant environment, slow world journey or reflective space chapter.
MUS-05.why: Among the lowest attack densities and brightness values in this folder, leaving room to test longer camera movements.
MUS-05.avoid: Low measured activity does not establish a specific ambient genre, instruments or absence of vocals.

MUS-06.direction: A large structure or industrial environment with a late change of scale.
MUS-06.why: A comparatively wide stereo image and a large late rise offer contrast for environment-to-detail travel.
MUS-06.avoid: The industrial direction is an editorial proposal, not identification of ship or metal recordings. Its steadiest passage still varies noticeably.

MUS-07.direction: A cinematic portfolio with genuinely different chapter intensities.
MUS-07.why: One of the largest loudness ranges and wider stereo images in the collection; a bounded middle passage is much steadier than the full source.
MUS-07.avoid: Do not choose it as background merely because the title says silent. Its full-file contrast is substantial.

MUS-08.direction: A short technology ad with material macros, clean specification changes and a resolved product ending.
MUS-08.why: One of the brighter non-vocal sources and a practical short duration for a single product story.
MUS-08.avoid: About 63 seconds total; a 120-second brief needs another arrangement or track. Busy passages still require SFX space.
MUS-08.history: Used in the original 45-second realme film, source 15–60s.

MUS-09.direction: A technical product reveal: mechanism, material, scale, then explanation.
MUS-09.why: A strong early measured rise can establish the product before a more controlled later specification passage.
MUS-09.avoid: Its stereo image is comparatively narrow. That is not a failed mono test, nor proof of phone-speaker performance.

MUS-10.direction: A vocal-led narrative, glitch montage or music-video treatment where the words carry the story.
MUS-10.why: User-provided timed lyrics confirm vocals and a narrative; the source also has the highest measured brightness in the folder.
MUS-10.avoid: Excluded by the user for earlier instrumental showcase work. Do not put under narration or use for unrelated product copy by default. The documented 42–54s bridge also includes vocal chops.
MUS-10.history: Timed vocal notes are supplied beside the MP3. Explicitly rejected as showreel music because of vocals.

MUS-11.direction: An isolation-to-reveal sequence with a clear dramatic turn rather than continuous fast cuts.
MUS-11.why: Sparse attack candidates and a very large local level rise give a practical contrast point to audition.
MUS-11.avoid: The steadiest 30-second passage is still variable. Do not promise an even narration bed from the title alone.

MUS-12.direction: A controlled editorial or lifestyle montage with readable captions.
MUS-12.why: Its least-variable passage is especially steady, allowing a test edit with longer holds and selective accents.
MUS-12.avoid: The night/lifestyle association is suggested by the name and editorial direction, not verified instrumentation. Vocals remain unverified.

MUS-13.direction: An architectural or material film that opens gradually and expands into a full room or object.
MUS-13.why: Low attack density and subdued brightness coexist with a large 16LU range and a substantial early rise.
MUS-13.avoid: A quiet-sounding title does not make the complete source a flat morning ambience. Choose a bounded section for voiceover.

MUS-14.direction: A graphic reel or feature montage built around large type and decisive scene changes.
MUS-14.why: High relative brightness, a clear early rise and relatively strong pulse autocorrelation give accents to audition for a driven edit.
MUS-14.avoid: The pulse estimate is not an approved beat grid; a prior beat-grid check failed. Do not snap edits automatically.
MUS-14.history: Used in the earlier 120-second realme extended edition, source 14–134s.

MUS-15.direction: Continuous spatial travel and big changes of scale, timed to evolving phrases instead of a beat grid.
MUS-15.why: A wide image, large dynamic range and extremely weak pulse autocorrelation support testing a freer camera-led edit.
MUS-15.avoid: The least-variable 30-second window is still highly variable. Not a first choice for an even background or rigid beat-synced kinetic reel.

MUS-16.direction: A more even process film, reflective editorial sequence or restrained background candidate.
MUS-16.why: The smallest full-track loudness range in the folder and subdued brightness make it worth auditioning when consistent levels matter.
MUS-16.avoid: An even level is not evidence of instrumental content or voiceover intelligibility. Do not expect a huge climax without checking a section.

MUS-17.direction: A structural or engineering story that moves between detail and scale.
MUS-17.why: Restrained spectral brightness, a large loudness range and a stable middle section provide two different editorial modes.
MUS-17.avoid: Not literal underwater or metal sound evidence. Keep mechanism SFX separate and leave their transients space.

MUS-18.direction: A space chapter with an expanding particle field or an environment reveal.
MUS-18.why: A wide stereo image, low brightness and substantial early level growth suggest long movement followed by an opening-out gesture.
MUS-18.avoid: Not a consistently silent bed; the full source spans almost 12LU. Treat particle hits selectively.

MUS-19.direction: A concise interface, craft-process or detailed product sequence.
MUS-19.why: High relative spectral brightness and a pronounced early rise offer positions for small graphic actions and a reveal.
MUS-19.avoid: The title does not prove that it is quiet click music. Its steadiest window is not especially even, and it lasts only about 69 seconds.

MUS-20.direction: A space/product hybrid with readable detail sections and a broader feature reveal.
MUS-20.why: Moderate brightness and a broad dynamic range support alternation between restrained detail and larger movement.
MUS-20.avoid: Keep narration tests section-specific; neither the title nor the meter establishes lack of vocals.
MUS-20.history: User-selected for the yellow realme reveal revision, source 18–138s, before Architects of Motion.

MUS-21.direction: A portfolio lift, opening title or closing reveal with a readable middle passage.
MUS-21.why: The early measured rise contrasts with a stable middle window; the relatively wide image can support a larger closing composition.
MUS-21.avoid: The name alone does not verify a warm or celebratory mood. About 91 seconds total, so it cannot fill two minutes unchanged.
MUS-21.history: Previously accepted by the user as a possible showcase track.

MUS-22.direction: A restrained orbit, slow product rotation or low-key spatial sequence.
MUS-22.why: Lowest full-track LUFS and spectral brightness in the collection, plus a comparatively small dynamic range.
MUS-22.avoid: Slow in the title is not a verified tempo. Dense micro-attacks can coexist with low brightness; do not mistake every detection for a cut cue.

MUS-23.direction: An initially controlled space/material chapter with an abrupt expansion later in the source.
MUS-23.why: Modest full-file loudness range conceals a very large local rise; that local contrast is more useful than the title for an edit.
MUS-23.avoid: Do not assume the middle is uniformly quiet. Audition the later rise before choosing a long passage.

MUS-24.direction: A dramatic long-form reveal or wide camera journey with substantial intensity changes.
MUS-24.why: Largest loudness range, widest measured stereo image and highest integrated loudness in this folder: this is a contrast candidate, not an automatic quiet bed.
MUS-24.avoid: Especially misleading title for background selection. Gain down, audition the exact range, and check any intended dialogue passage.

MUS-25.direction: A minimal material/architectural opening that grows into a more substantial scene.
MUS-25.why: Low brightness and attack density combined with a very large early level rise support contrast between negative space and developed artwork.
MUS-25.avoid: Not a flat white-room ambience throughout; the full source has almost 13LU of range.
